info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package studio is Hanzo Studio's workflow backend: every creation — an image, a poster, a document, a deck, a type system, a 3D model, an ad, a film, a voice, a song — is a run of a graph of steps that the person who started it owns.

post.summary: One chat turn that plans and launches runs, streamed
post.description:
Sends one message in a thread (a new thread when `thread` is absent). The assistant answers in text and, when the message asks for something to be made, plans it as runs and starts them; each is exactly the run POST /v1/studio/runs would start, checked and paid for the same way.

Answers text/event-stream: `thread` {thread} first; `delta` {text} as the answer is written; `run` {seq, run} for each run the turn started (follow it on its own events); `error` (a problem document) when a planned run could not start — a wallet that cannot cover it is status 402 — and the turn goes on; `done` {thread, message, runs} last, with the stored message. 402 before the stream when the wallet cannot pay for the turn itself.

post.summary: The render lane's door, for Studio's render workers alone
post.description: The CPU render workers claim render jobs here, heartbeat them, ask for the upload of the one file a job makes, and complete or fail them: the durable engine's own activity verbs, for the render lane only. Admits the render workload's identity and answers 403 to every other caller, a person included.

post.summary: Starts a run: name exactly one of template, flow or graph, with the input its inputs schema asks for.
post.description:
Starts a run: name exactly one of template, flow or graph, with the input its
inputs schema asks for. The run is checked, priced and its estimate reserved
against your org's wallet, then queued; the answer is the run at queued. Follow
it on GET /v1/studio/runs/{id}/events.

parent makes this run the next version of that run: it takes the parent's graph
and input, overlaid by what this request states. Send Idempotency-Key to make a
retried request start one run, not two. 402 when the wallet cannot cover the
estimate; 422 when the graph or input does not validate.

get.summary: Stream a run's progress as Server-Sent Events
get.description:
Holds text/event-stream open on one run you may read and writes one frame per change until the run ends, then a final `done` frame, and closes. Every frame carries `id:`, the event's sequence number in the run, so a client that reconnects with Last-Event-ID (or ?after=) receives exactly what it missed. A run that already ended replays its events and closes.

Frames (`event:` name, `data:` JSON): `run` {seq, run} on a status change; `step` {seq, run, step} when a step's status, attempt or progress moves; `asset` {seq, run, step, asset} when an output lands, as its Library item with fresh signed URLs; `log` {seq, run, step, text}; `done` {seq, run} when the run ended (succeeded, failed or canceled). Each carries the run, step or asset as it is now. A `: ping` comment every 15 seconds keeps intermediaries from closing the stream.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer` (a fetch-based reader; a browser EventSource cannot set it) or the session cookie. 404 for a run you may not read; 429 when your org already holds 64 streams.

(402 when it cannot be); 409 while the run is still going or once it succeeded.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

name.description: Name is the device, as its worker reports it.

owner.description: Owner is org (linked by your org with hanzo link) or platform.

seen.description: Seen is its worker's last heartbeat.

status.description: Status is idle, busy or offline.

steps.description: Steps are the graph's steps, 1 to 64 of them.

url.description: URL opens the file inline; Download saves it; Preview is its still.

runs.description: Runs are the runs this message started.

charged_cents.description: ChargedCents is what the finished steps cost; final once the run ends.

estimate_cents.description: EstimateCents is what was reserved when the run started.

input.description: Input is what the run was given, as its inputs schema reads it.

outputs.description: Outputs are the Library items the run made, the final steps' first.

root.description: Root is the first version's id; equal to id on version 1.

text.description: Text is the last chat step's text, when the run's product is words.

brand.description: Brand is a brand id; its tokens are brand.* in the graph.

input.description: Input are the values the inputs schema asks for.

parent.description: Parent makes this run the next version of that run.

each.description:
Each fans the step out: a {{path}} naming an array, run once per item (at
most 64), its outputs the items' outputs in order.

id.description:
ID names the step within its graph: a lowercase letter, then up to 31
lowercase letters, digits or underscores.

op.description:
Op is what the step does: chat, image.generate, image.edit, voice.speak,
music.generate, video.generate, model.generate, studio.render, render.html,
render.document, render.slides, render.composition or video.edit.

title.description: Title is what a person sees for the step.

with.description: With are the op's parameters. Values may reference other steps.

attempt.description: Attempt is how many times the step has started.

executor.description: Executor is where the step runs: gateway, studio.render, render or flow.run.

items.description: Items is how many items a step with each fanned out to.

message.description: Message is what the step is doing now, for a person.

outputs.description: Outputs are the Library item ids the step made.

status.description: Status is pending, queued, running, succeeded, failed, canceled or skipped.

id.description: ID is a catalog slug (image, poster) or an org template's id.

preview.description: Preview is an asset id or https URL of a still that shows what it makes.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
